# Muse Douyin data and download tools

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

`douyin_download` accepts a selected official HTTPS video/share `url`, or a checked `urls` list, and writes verified media into the initiating session's `source/media/douyin/` directory. Public requests always ignore saved browser settings. `publicOnly:true` disables the internal-browser fallback. No browser profile, Cookie file, remembered account or arbitrary output directory is accepted by the tool.

## Runtime and configuration

The packaged integration requires Desktop Host protocol 6 and `douyinBrowser.version === 3` for page data and internal-browser acquisition. The download tool also accepts the existing version 2 download service. Installing the plugin alone does not add the browser transport. Desktop selects its validated bundled Python automatically, preserves explicit media executables, and discovers existing ffmpeg/ffprobe from the bundled media directory or ordinary PATH without installing packages or changing PATH. Mac installers include architecture-matched media executables; runtime discovery does not install dependencies. Packaged Python scripts and their extractor archive reside outside ASAR so the bundled interpreter can open them.

The public runner requires `agents`, `tools` and `subprocess`; browser fallback additionally uses the Host-owned transport. Deployment settings remain `pythonExecutable`, `ffprobeExecutable`, `ffmpegExecutable`, `settingsHome`, `requestTimeoutMs`, `timeoutMs`, `maxDownloadBytes`, `graceMs`, `maxVideos`, `dataTimeoutMs`, and `maxComments`. Runner defaults are 120 seconds, 512 MiB and 20 links; page-data defaults are 30 seconds per link and 20 comments per page. `requestTimeoutMs` also allows delivery of the page result before the outer transport deadline. `maxDownloadBytes` (1 byte to 8 GiB) applies to public acquisition, internal-browser transfer and native-file verification. Internal-browser transfers allow one active task and 120 seconds including preparation. Missing verification executables return a blocked result.

## Page data and optional downloads

`douyin_data` accepts either `url` or `urls`, within `maxVideos`, and reads each selected work in order. `source` is `public`, `creator`, or `auto`; every successful result identifies `public-page` or `creator-page` and its observation time. Creator data requires normal login and evidence associating the exact work with that account. A browser login does not grant OAuth API scopes. `auto` uses the public page. `creator` opens the normal Creator content-management page and requires a matching string work ID, its aligned modification permission and the same ID in its statistics. It reads only the selected row; a missing verified own-work association returns `CREATOR_OWNERSHIP_UNVERIFIED`. Complete normal page loading or navigate to older works when needed. Public data does not substitute for unavailable creator data.

The five counters are plays, likes, comments, shares and favorites. Each counter reports an exact number, a rounded display, or `null` with a reason. Public counters come from the exact normal page detail response, its initial data, or the unique visible work action strip; exposed positive play counts are retained; missing values and placeholder zero remain unavailable. `includeComments:true` requests one observed page, bounded by `commentLimit` and `maxComments`; `commentCursor` applies to one selected link only. The total comment count is independent of returned comment items. The Desktop provider returns `COMMENTS_UNAVAILABLE` for comment content and pagination; it preserves observed counters and marks the result partial. The data format supports bounded comment text, comment IDs and numeric counts without account identifiers or credentials.

`download:true` acquires each selected work through the existing downloader, using its validated canonical URL when page data already resolved a share link and includes a separate download result. A failed download preserves available data; unavailable data can accompany a verified download. Batch results are `complete`, `partial` or `blocked`, with each item kept in input order. Cancellation joins the admitted browser read or child process, retains already observed data in the logged cancellation result and prevents the next link from starting. Page reads need no Python or media executables. Data remains in the model-visible, persisted tool result; this tool does not create another statistics file.

## Internal playback and results

After a public access failure, MUSE opens the official page in the existing isolated Browser panel for the currently selected Session. The user performs ordinary login, verification and playback. The initiating tool call starts the exact video download automatically after the initial main-document navigation finishes; playback inspection also waits for main-document loading to finish. Failed playback inspection, DNS resolution, staging and native download initiation return separate blocked codes. Official Douyin video and Creator tabs retain login per workspace across application restarts; unrelated browser tabs use process-local storage. The downloader does not access external browser databases, export session credentials, manufacture signatures or bypass access controls, CAPTCHA or DRM.

The transport identifies media by either `player-exact` (target-specific public `_ROUTER_DATA` or bounded player-parent `awemeInfo` properties, paired with the exact visible player's successful MP4 source), or `provider-detail-verified` (a page-generated official target detail JSON response, exact work ID, bounded plain MP4 addresses and matching visible-player duration). The latter observes only the main document's successful target response and reports `currentSrcMatched:false`; it never rewrites signed URLs or makes an API request. CDN requests and redirects require public DNS results from the leased browser network context. Ordinary same-origin blob playback may establish provider duration, while the downloaded address must remain a plain HTTPS MP4 from the exact official detail response. The player-exact branch rejects blob sources. Public player properties accept string addresses or `{src}` entries. A paused player remains eligible after media data has loaded; acquisition does not change playback. A player-added `__vid` must equal the exact string work ID and be the only difference from a supplied address; the native transfer retains the unchanged visible source. The current document retains at most 16 successful MP4 response addresses from media or XHR requests; playback selects only its exact observed source and document replacement clears those addresses. Missing metadata, recommendations, protected media, media fragments and ambiguous associations are unsupported. Observation of 200/206 does not indicate a complete download. A one-use Host/owner/Session/task/lease/target authorization enables only the exact native attempt; generic browser downloads remain rejected. Session switching, document replacement, page closure, expiry, cancellation and Host disconnect revoke it and cancel verification.

Success requires actual nonzero bytes within the bound, ffprobe video/duration/dimension checks, complete ffmpeg decoding and SHA-256. Provider-selected files must also match the detail response's duration (within 0.25 seconds) and aspect ratio (within 1%). A source receipt includes the public video page, task/target IDs, bytes, duration, dimensions, identification method, a media hostname and hashed transient URL; it never includes Cookie, Authorization or signed media URLs. Files are published without overwriting existing output. `STAGED` is transport completion only, not the tool's downloaded result. Batches return `complete`, `partial` or `blocked` per verified item.

## Validation and packaging

Run `node --test tests/*.test.js` and `node scripts/pack.mjs --out /absolute/output/directory`. The tarball includes the canonical locked public Python extractor, but depends on the matching Host patch for internal-browser acquisition. The keyless page-data fixture uses authored counts and transport results; it does not establish live public or creator availability. The [blocked-batch Session replay](../../../snapshots/session/muse-douyin-blocked-batch/snapshot.yml) exercises the real tool and agent loop with isolated acquisition failures and preserves per-item diagnostics. Offline and synthetic media tests do not establish that the live acceptance URL can download. Live acceptance requires normal playback and a file-backed verified receipt for that URL.
